subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Structure 1.4 Counting particles by mass: the mole

questions.q: Avogadro's constant is approximately:
questions.explain: One mole contains 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

questions.q: The molar mass of a substance is:
options: The mass of one mole in grams, numerically equal to its relative formula mass
questions.explain: Molar mass (g/mol) is numerically equal to the relative atomic or formula mass.

questions.q: How many moles are in 36 g of water (Mr of H2O = 18)?
questions.explain: moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol.

questions.q: How many molecules are in 0.5 mol of carbon dioxide?
questions.explain: number = moles × Avogadro's constant = 0.5 × 6.02 x 10^23 = 3.01 x 10^23.

questions.q: A compound contains 40% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its empirical formula is:
questions.explain: Dividing by atomic masses gives a 1:2:1 ratio of C:H:O, so the empirical formula is CH2O.

questions.q: The empirical formula of a compound shows:
options: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms
The actual number of atoms in a molecule
questions.explain: The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.

questions.q: What mass of NaOH (Mr = 40) is needed to make 500 cm3 of a 0.100 mol/dm3 solution?
Concentration in mol/dm3 is calculated as:
options: Moles of solute ÷ volume of solution in dm3
questions.explain: Concentration = n ÷ V, with volume in cubic decimetres (litres).

questions.q: The ideal gas equation is:
questions.explain: P is pressure, V volume, n moles, R the gas constant and T the absolute temperature.

questions.q: In the ideal gas equation, the temperature T must be expressed in:
questions.explain: Absolute temperature in kelvin is required; K = °C + 273.

questions.q: At constant temperature, if the pressure on a fixed mass of gas is doubled, its volume will:
questions.explain: Boyle's law: at constant T, P and V are inversely proportional.

questions.q: At constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is doubled. The absolute temperature must have:
questions.explain: Charles's law: at constant P, V is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.q: Equal volumes of different gases at the same temperature and pressure contain:
questions.explain: This is Avogadro's law, a consequence of the ideal gas model.

questions.q: Real gases deviate most from ideal behaviour at:
questions.explain: Under these conditions particle volume and intermolecular forces become significant.

questions.q: In the reaction N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, how many moles of ammonia form from 3 mol of nitrogen (excess hydrogen)?
questions.explain: The mole ratio N2:NH3 is 1:2, so 3 mol N2 gives 6 mol NH3.

questions.q: The limiting reactant in a reaction is the one that:
options: Is completely used up first, determining the amount of product
questions.explain: The limiting reactant runs out first and sets the maximum yield.

questions.q: If the theoretical yield is 8.0 g and the actual yield is 6.0 g, the percentage yield is:
questions.explain: % yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100 = (6.0 ÷ 8.0) × 100 = 75%.

questions.q: A sample contains 0.25 mol of an ideal gas. At the same T and P, a 0.50 mol sample of a different gas would occupy:
questions.explain: At fixed T and P, volume is proportional to the number of moles (Avogadro's law).

questions.q: The molecular formula differs from the empirical formula in that it shows:
options: The actual number of each type of atom in a molecule
questions.explain: For example, empirical CH2O corresponds to molecular C6H12O6 for glucose.

questions.q: According to kinetic theory, the average kinetic energy of gas particles depends on:
questions.explain: Average kinetic energy is proportional to temperature in kelvin, independent of gas identity.
